trust_decision.summary: The router's per-method tree cache must be a prototype-less map so that a request method naming an inherited Object.prototype property (e.g. 'constructor') misses and falls through to defaultRoute/null instead of yielding a non-tree and throwing; decided by replacing `this.trees = {}` with `Object.create(null)` at both places the map is produced (index.js:105 construction, index.js:470 reset).

landing_point.why: The report says DDoS over HTTP/2; an engineer starts at `lookup` -> `find`, where `this.trees[method]` is indexed and only checked with `=== undefined` (index.js:568-569), so an inherited key is treated as a live tree and `currentNode.prefix.length` throws.

fix_sites.entry_point: FindMyWay() constructor; every request path that follows (lookup -> find, find, findRoute, hasRoute, prettyPrint)
reset() public API, and off()/addConstraintStrategy() -> _rebuild -> reset (index.js:529, index.js:466, index.js:744-745)
fix_sites.module_kind: core implementation (save/reload path that re-creates the map)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: reset() looks like a state-clearing helper on a different path from request dispatch, and a fix verified on a freshly constructed router never executes index.js:470, so a solver can argue the reload path is already covered by the constructor.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unknown-method requests must keep falling back to defaultRoute and find() must keep returning null instead of throwing (an allowlist/throw-based hardening breaks this), and `router.trees` must stay a string-keyed serialisable map because prettyPrint's merged tree reads `mergedRouter.trees.MERGED` (index.js:807) and the router-equality helpers compare JSON.stringify(router.trees) (test/find-route.test.js:10, test/has-route.test.js:10); reset() must also still clear every method.

O6_input_shapes: method string equal to any inherited Object.prototype property name: 'constructor', '__proto__', 'toString', 'valueOf', 'hasOwnProperty', 'isPrototypeOf', 'propertyIsEnumerable', 'toLocaleString', '__defineGetter__' (exact lowercase only; 'CONSTRUCTOR' already misses)
the same name arriving as req.method through lookup() with headers {'}:authority'...} (HTTP/2 shape) and as a direct find(method, path) argument
the same name through findRoute()/hasRoute() rather than find()
the same name after a reset()/off() rebuild, when the map has been re-created

O7_producer.where: index.js:470 (reset, reached from _rebuild at index.js:744-745); map first produced at index.js:105

O8_uncovered_routes.route: findRoute(method, path) indexes this.trees[method] with only an `=== undefined` check, then reads currentNode.prefix, so method 'constructor' throws
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: findRoute/hasRoute are for route inspection, not request dispatch; the report and its example test only exercise request-time lookup, so these can be called developer-facing and not attacker-reachable.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~250 lines from find(); no package boundary

O8_uncovered_routes.route: hasRoute(method, path) delegates to findRoute and inherits the same crash for an inherited method name
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a one-line wrapper around findRoute; a solver who fixes find() counts it as already covered by the shared helper.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: prettyPrint({method}) reads this.trees[method] and treats an inherited property as a tree instead of returning '(empty tree)'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a debugging helper, not reachable from a request, so it looks outside the reported DoS.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second name -> store map (`constrainedHandlerStores`) indexed with a free-form constraint name in generated code (lib/handler-storage.js:150)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: constraint strategy names are arbitrary strings accepted at lib/constrainer.js:40-54, so a maintainer adding another per-name map would plausibly write `{}` again and hit the same inherited-key collision.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the staticChildren map, currently keyed by a single char from path.charAt() (lib/node.js:38), could be keyed by a multi-char path label
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: prefix-keyed child maps are a natural optimisation for this radix tree (it already keys by path.charAt(0) at lib/node.js:63), and a longer label makes names like 'constructor' indexable.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: `this.strategies[name]` lookups for a caller-supplied constraint name (lib/constrainer.js:31, lib/constrainer.js:108)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: hasConstraintStrategy()/validateConstraints() already take an arbitrary name from the caller, so a maintainer could add a method- or header-keyed strategy map alongside them.

O9_family: prototype-key / inherited-property confusion in a plain-object method map (CWE-1321 class), leading to an uncaught TypeError

O10_build.toolchain: npm; borp (node:test runner); standard (lint); tsd (types); no native/gyp steps
O10_build.project_tests: `npm test` = standard + borp + tsd over test/; method-dispatch coverage lives in test/methods.test.js:694-740 ('Unsupported method' lookup/find family) and test/http2/constraint.host.test.js

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: guard only the reproduced call site — add `Object.hasOwn(this.trees, method)` / a hardcoded 'constructor' deny-list at index.js:568 — leaving findRoute, hasRoute, prettyPrint and the reset() rebuild on the plain-object map.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/constrainer.js keeps `this.strategies` as a plain object and resolves caller-supplied names with `this.strategies[key]` (lib/constrainer.js:31,44,108), so a constraint literally named 'constructor' passes validateConstraints and yields a broken derive function; a related plain-object-key issue but a different sink from the method->tree map in this advisory, so not pursued.
